question:
After an HLA-mismatched allogeneic HCT, a T-cell clone is isolated from the recipient. The clone does not react to intact donor cells. It responds only when recipient antigen-presenting cells present a peptide derived from the mismatched donor HLA-DR protein in the groove of the recipient's own HLA molecules.
Does this clone exhibit indirect T-cell allorecognition? (Yes/No)
atom_statement: T-cell allorecognition can be either direct or indirect.
evidence: T-cell allorecognition can be either direct SBT sequencing-based typing (Sanger sequencing), NGS or indirect.

question:
What is the target of direct T-cell alloreactivity?
A) Intact mismatched HLA–peptide complexes retained inside the cytoplasm of allogeneic cells
B) Intact mismatched HLA–peptide complexes expressed on the cell surface of allogeneic cells
C) Processed peptides derived from mismatched HLA proteins, expressed on the cell surface of allogeneic cells
D) Intact HLA–peptide complexes of matched HLA, expressed on the cell surface of allogeneic cells
atom_statement: Direct T-cell alloreactivity is targeted to intact mismatched HLA–peptide complexes expressed on the cell surface of allogeneic cells.
evidence: Direct T-cell alloreactivity is targeted next-generation sequencing to intact mismatched HLA–peptide complexes expressed on the cell surface of allogeneic cells and can be mediated by both naïve and memory T cells (Archbold et al. 2008).

question: In HLA-matched allogeneic HCT, which antigens are the only targets of T-cell alloreactivity?
atom_statement: In HLA-matched allo-HCT, minor histocompatibility antigens (mHAgs) are the only targets of T-cell alloreactivity.
evidence: These peptides are referred to as minor histocompatibility antigens (mHAgs) (Spierings 2014); mHAgs are the only targets of T-cell alloreactivity in HLA-matched allo-HCT and are mainly recognized by naïve T cells.

question:
A recipient and donor are HLA-identical siblings undergoing allogeneic HCT. The recipient carries a polymorphic variant of an intracellular protein that the donor lacks. A peptide from this variant is presented on the shared HLA-A*02:01 molecule and is recognized by donor T cells. Investigators find that the responding T cells are predominantly antigen-experienced memory T cells (CD45RO+).
Is this the T-cell subset by which this type of antigen is mainly recognized? (Yes/No)
atom_statement: Minor histocompatibility antigens (mHAgs) are mainly recognized by naïve T cells.
evidence: These peptides are referred to as minor histocompatibility antigens (mHAgs) (Spierings 2014); mHAgs are the only targets of T-cell alloreactivity in HLA-matched allo-HCT and are mainly recognized by naïve T cells.
